'''CorusMall''' was a trade center located not far from the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].

==Description==
[[File:CorusMallStoreroom-TPMVG.png|thumb|right|175px|The Roonan owner on CorusMall's storeroom in 32 BBY.]]
CorusMall was a trade center run by [[Roonan/Legends|Roonan]] traders, which included a storeroom, main trading hall, a platform with four [[Turbolift/Legends|lift tubes]], and a docking plataform outside. The Roonans sold different goods from across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], including some collectibles from all over the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]], and food like the best brand of [[chokie]] imported all the way from [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].

==History==
[[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Quarsh Panaka]] visited CorusMall in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] while [[Skirmish at Coruscant|searching]] through [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] for the kidnapped [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Queen Amidala]]. After being attacked by some [[Coruscant mercenary|mercenaries]] led by a [[Thug leader|Sun Guard]], Panaka sneaked in CorusMall storeroom where the Roonan owner told him to leave. He then moved onto the main trading hall, where the present Roonan traders told him that a group of thugs used one of the lift tubes and took Amidala with them to the [[Restricted Area|lower levels]] of the city.

==Behind the scenes==
CorusMall appears on the "Coruscant" level of [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''The Phantom Menace'' video game]], released in [[1999]]. However, the events of this level contradict [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|the movie]] storyline since the Queen was never kidnapped, but instead traveled safely to the [[500 Republica/Legends|500 Republica]].

The sign "CorusMall" is written in [[High Galactic/Legends|High Galactic alphabet]], which is different and more rarely used than the most common [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]] system. Some glass cases from stores in the mall also have High Galactic writings.
